The straight-line distance between the boat and the lighthouse is \({@distInit@}m\).


(a) Given that the angle of {@angTypeA@} between the {@if angTypeA="depression" then "lighthouse and the boat" else if angTypeA="elevation" then "boat and the lighthouse"@} is \({@angInit@}^\circ\), find the height of the lighthouse above sea level.
Give your answer to the nearest whole metre.

[[input:ans1]] \(m\) [[validation:ans1]]

(2)

[[feedback:prt1]]


(b) The boat moves \({@distChange@}m\) away from the lighthouse (directly right in the diagram). At this point, what is the angle of {@angTypeB@} between the {@if angTypeB="depression" then "lighthouse and the boat" else if angTypeB="elevation" then "boat and the lighthouse"@}?
Give your answer to 2dp.

[[input:ans2]] \(^\circ\) [[validation:ans2]]

truefeedback.text:
Here is a worked solution:

The measurements given can be related with a right-angled triangle:

[[jsxgraph height="200px" width="200px"]] JXG.Options.text.useMathJax=true; var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingBox:[-5,5,5,-5], showCopyright:false, showNavigation:false, keepaspectratio:true }); var pointStyle = { fixed:true, visible:false }; var P1 = board.create("point", [-3,4], pointStyle); var P2 = board.create("point", [-3,-4], pointStyle); var P3 = board.create("point", [3,-4], pointStyle); var P4 = board.create("point", [0,4], pointStyle); var segmentStyle = { fixed:true, highlight:false, label:{ fixed:true, highlight:false, fontSize:15, offset:[0,0], useMathJax:true, parse:false } }; segmentStyle.dash = 4; board.create("segment", [P2, P3], segmentStyle); board.create("segment", [P1, P4], segmentStyle); segmentStyle.dash = "none"; segmentStyle.withLabel = true; segmentStyle.name = "\\(".concat({#distInit#},"m\\)"); segmentStyle.label.offset = [10,10]; board.create("segment", [P1, P3], segmentStyle); segmentStyle.name = "\\(h\\)"; segmentStyle.label.offset = [-30,0]; board.create("segment", [P1, P2], segmentStyle); var angleStyle = { fixed:true, highlight:false, radius:1.5, name:"\\(".concat({#angInit#},"^\\circ\\)"), label:{ fixed:true, highlight:false, strokeColor:"black", fontSize:12, offset:[0,-5], anchorX:"left", useMathJax:true, parse:false } }; board.create("angle", [P3, P1, P4], angleStyle); angleStyle.label.anchorX = "right"; board.create("angle", [P1, P3, P2], angleStyle); [[/jsxgraph]]

Therefore, by using \(\sin(\theta) = \frac{o}{h}\)

\(\sin({@angInit@}) = \frac{h}{{@distInit@}}\)

\(h = \sin({@angInit@}) \times {@distInit@}\)

\(h = {@decimalplaces(tans1,5)@}...\)

\(h = {@round(tans1)@}m\) (to the nearest whole metre)

You have found the height of the lighthouse above sea level.
However, you have not rounded your answer correctly to the nearest metre.

You have not used the correct trigonometric function to relate the height, angle and straight-line distance given.

The height of the lighthouse is opposite the angle of {@angTypeA@}, so you should use \(\sin(\theta) = \frac{o}{h}\)

Here is a worked solution:

Using either trigonometry or Pythagoras' theorem, we can calculate the initial horizontal distance between the base of the cliff and the boat.

\(d = {@distInit@} \times \cos({@angInit@})\)

\(d = {@decimalplaces(distInit*cos(angInit*(%pi/180)),5)@}...\)


Now, you can relate the new horizontal distance and the height from part (a) to find the purple angle \(\theta\).

\(\tan(\theta) = \frac{o}{a}\)

\(\tan(\theta) = \frac{{@decimalplaces(tans1,5)@}...}{{@distChange@} + {@decimalplaces(distInit*cos(angInit*(%pi/180)),5)@}...}\)

\(\tan(\theta) = {@decimalplaces(tans1/(distChange + distInit*cos(angInit*(%pi/180))),5)@}...\)

\(\theta = {@decimalplaces(tansA2,5)@}...\)

\(\theta = {@decimalplaces(tansA2,2)@}^\circ\) (2dp)

However, your answer is consistent with the height you gave in part (a).

You have also not rounded your answer correctly to 1dp.

You have not used the correct trigonometric function to find the {@if abs(ans2-(atan(ans1/(distInit*sin(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange))*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(atan(tans1/(distInit*sin(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange))*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(atan(ans1/(distInit*tan(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange))*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(atan(tans1/(distInit*tan(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange))*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(atan((distInit*sin(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange)/ans1)*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(atan((distInit*sin(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange)/tans1)*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(atan((distInit*tan(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange)/ans1)*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(atan((distInit*tan(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange)/tans1)*180/%pi))<=0.1 then "initial horizontal distance from the boat to the cliff using the angle and straight-line distance given." else if abs(ans2-(asin(ans1/(distInit*cos(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange))*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(asin(tans1/(distInit*cos(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange))*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(acos(ans1/(distInit*cos(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange))*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(acos(tans1/(distInit*cos(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange))*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(asin((distInit*cos(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange)/ans1)*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(asin((distInit*cos(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange)/tans1)*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(acos((distInit*cos(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange)/ans1)*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(acos((distInit*cos(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange)/tans1)*180/%pi))<=0.1 then sconcat("angle of ", angTypeB, " using the horizontal distance from the boat to the cliff and the height of the lighthouse.")@}

You should have related these using {@if abs(ans2-(atan(ans1/(distInit*sin(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange))*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(atan(tans1/(distInit*sin(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange))*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(atan(ans1/(distInit*tan(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange))*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(atan(tans1/(distInit*tan(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange))*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(atan((distInit*sin(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange)/ans1)*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(atan((distInit*sin(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange)/tans1)*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(atan((distInit*tan(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange)/ans1)*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(atan((distInit*tan(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange)/tans1)*180/%pi))<=0.1 then "\\(\\cos(\\theta) = \\frac{a}{h}\\)" else if abs(ans2-(asin(ans1/(distInit*cos(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange))*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(asin(tans1/(distInit*cos(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange))*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(acos(ans1/(distInit*cos(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange))*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(acos(tans1/(distInit*cos(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange))*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(asin((distInit*cos(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange)/ans1)*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(asin((distInit*cos(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange)/tans1)*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(acos((distInit*cos(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange)/ans1)*180/%pi))<=0.1 or abs(ans2-(acos((distInit*cos(angInit*%pi/180)+distChange)/tans1)*180/%pi))<=0.1 then "\\(\\tan(\\theta) = \\frac{o}{a}\\)"@}

You have not used the correct trigonometric function to find the initial horizontal distance from the boat to the cliff using the angle and straight-line distance given.

You should have related these using \(\cos(\theta) = \frac{a}{h}\)

You have also used the wrong function to find the angle of {@angTypeB@} using the horizontal distance from the boat to the cliff and the height of the lighthouse.

You should have related these using \(\tan(\theta) = \frac{o}{a}\)
